objects.name: Analytic 1898
objects.description: Configured Windows object-access monitoring identifies a write to an Industrial Control System (ICS) engineering project file by a process that is not the recognized vendor engineering software, or by the vendor engineering software immediately after loading a project file from an untrusted source. Documented mechanism in Havex (trojanized vendor software/installers distributed via compromised vendor websites). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance. Collection requirement: use Windows Security Event ID 4663 with Object Access auditing and SACLs on approved project repositories; Sysmon FileCreate events can corroborate writes/overwrites but do not report generic file-open/read activity.

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: WinEventLog:Security
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Windows Security Event ID 4663 (requires Object Access auditing/SACL): engineering process reads/opens project file from unapproved repository/removable-media/network-share path

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational Event ID 11 FileCreate/overwrite or Event ID 2 FileCreateTime, as applicable: Engineering tool process opens project file from path not in approved project repository (removable media, email attachment cache, untrusted network share)
